## How it works

1. **Learn**Read, play and watch. Everything in Learn is free and open to everyone.
2. **Pass the final**Each item has a short final. Questions are different every time and graded on our side.
3. **Get credits**Passing adds credits straight to your workspace balance.

## The fine print, in plain words

- Credits land in your workspace balance and work for anything you run on MIOSA, including Optimal.
- They expire 180 days after you earn them.
- The limit is $100 per person and $100 per organization, for life.
- You need a verified email and an account at least a day old. If you pass before that, the reward waits and arrives on its own.
- Finals draw new questions each time and are graded by us. After a miss you wait a little before trying again.
- The person must complete it themselves. No AI agents, scripts or other people.
- Videos count when you watch them at normal speed in a visible tab. Skipping ahead does not count.
- Credits cannot be withdrawn or refunded to a card.

learn/first-production-app:
This tutorial takes a small Next.js application from an empty Sandbox to a verified production URL. You will create a Sandbox, write the app, review a temporary Preview, publish an immutable Version, verify the stable Deployment URL, connect `app.example.com`, and learn rollback before you need it. Do it now Deploy your first app Turn a repo or a sandbox into a stable production URL with immutable versions and rollback. - [New deployment](https://miosa.ai/deploy/new): (opens the MIOSA console in a new tab) miosa deploy create --from-sandbox my-box --wait Publish a sandbox, a git repo (--git) or a local directory (--dir). Add --type docker_deploy for App Engine. Next [Publishing guide](/docs/docker-host/publishing) > **Note: What this tutorial preserves** > > Publishing does not destroy or convert the Sandbox. > The Sandbox remains a development environment, while the Release and Deployment become independent production resources. ## What you will create | Resource | Example | Purpose | |---|---|---| | Sandbox | `hello-nextjs` | Mutable place to create and test the application. | | Preview | API-returned temporary URL | Review the live development server before publishing. | | Deployment | `hello-nextjs` | Stable production identity and version history. | | Platform URL | API-returned `public_url` | Immediate production access without customer DNS. | | Custom domain | `app.example.com` | Optional customer-owned hostname attached to the Deployment. | ## Before you start You need: - A MIOSA User with access to the intended Organization and Workspace. - A workspace API key stored only in a server or terminal environment. - The MIOSA CLI installed (v2.2 or later). - Permission to create Sandboxes, publish Deployments, and configure domains. - Access to the DNS provider only if you complete the custom-domain section. ```bash export MIOSA_API_KEY="msk_u_..." miosa whoami ``` Confirm that the response identifies the expected Organization and Workspace before creating anything. > **Caution: Do not continue in the wrong Organization** > > Resource IDs are not a substitute for checking the active customer boundary. > If the CLI reports the wrong Organization or Workspace, correct that context before creating the Sandbox or Deployment. ## Step 1: Create the Sandbox **CLI** ```bash miosa create hello-nextjs \ --template nextjs \ --ttl 1h \ --wait \ --json ``` Save the returned Sandbox id: ```bash export SANDBOX_ID="" ``` **TypeScript** ```typescript import { Miosa } from "@miosa/sdk"; const miosa = new Miosa({ apiKey: process.env.MIOSA_API_KEY! }); const sandbox = await miosa.sandboxes.create({ name: "hello-nextjs", templateId: "nextjs", }); console.log(sandbox.id); ``` **Python** ```python import os from miosa import Miosa miosa = Miosa(api_key=os.environ["MIOSA_API_KEY"]) sandbox = miosa.sandboxes.create(name="hello-nextjs", template_id="nextjs") print(sandbox.id) ``` **Expected result:** the Sandbox reaches a usable running state. If creation remains pending, inspect the returned capacity or readiness reason before retrying. Do not create repeated Sandboxes while the first request is still progressing. ## Step 2: Create the Next.js application Scaffold the app inside the Sandbox, then replace `app/page.tsx`. **CLI** ```bash miosa exec hello-nextjs --cwd /workspace -- bash -lc 'pnpm create next-app@latest hello-nextjs --typescript --eslint --app --no-tailwind --use-pnpm --yes' ``` Write the page file locally, then copy it into the Sandbox: ```bash miosa files cp ./page.tsx hello-nextjs:/workspace/hello-nextjs/app/page.tsx ``` Build it: ```bash miosa exec hello-nextjs --cwd /workspace/hello-nextjs --timeout 300 -- pnpm build ``` **TypeScript** ```typescript const page = `export default function Home() { return (

Deployed with MIOSA

Hello from MIOSA

); }`; await sandbox.exec.run( "cd /workspace && pnpm create next-app@latest hello-nextjs --typescript --eslint --app --no-tailwind --use-pnpm --yes", ); await sandbox.files.write("/workspace/hello-nextjs/app/page.tsx", page); for await (const event of sandbox.exec.stream( "cd /workspace/hello-nextjs && pnpm build", )) { console.log(event); } ``` **Python** ```python page = '''export default function Home() { return (

Hello from MIOSA

); }''' sandbox.exec.run( "cd /workspace && pnpm create next-app@latest hello-nextjs --typescript --eslint --app --no-tailwind --use-pnpm --yes", ) sandbox.files.write_file("/workspace/hello-nextjs/app/page.tsx", page) for event in sandbox.exec_stream("cd /workspace/hello-nextjs && pnpm build"): print(event) ``` **Expected result:** the build command exits with status `0` and Next.js reports a successful build. ## Step 3: Start and preview the application Start the server as a background process so it keeps running after the CLI disconnects, then expose port 3000. **CLI** ```bash miosa process start hello-nextjs \ --name web \ --cwd /workspace/hello-nextjs \ -- pnpm start --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000 miosa preview create hello-nextjs 3000 --name web --json ``` **TypeScript** ```typescript const preview = await sandbox.previews.create(3000); console.log(preview.url); ``` **Python** ```python preview = sandbox.previews.create(port=3000, label="app") print(preview["url"]) ``` Open the exact Preview URL returned by MIOSA. **Expected result:** the page displays "Hello from MIOSA." > **Tip: Preview is not production** > > The Preview reflects the current Sandbox process and files. > It can change immediately and can disappear when the Sandbox stops. > The stable production URL is created during publishing. ## Step 4: Publish a Deployment `miosa deploy create` publishes a new Deployment and makes it live. Give it the Sandbox as its source, the path the app lives at inside the Sandbox, and the command that serves it. **CLI** ```bash miosa deploy create \ --from-sandbox hello-nextjs \ --name hello-nextjs \ --dir /workspace/hello-nextjs \ --port 3000 \ --run-command "pnpm start --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000" \ --wait \ --json ``` Add `--type docker_deploy` to publish through Docker Host instead of the default runtime. Save these values from the response: ```bash export DEPLOYMENT_ID="" export PUBLIC_URL="" ``` **TypeScript** ```typescript const result = await sandbox.deploy({ name: "hello-nextjs", path: "/workspace/hello-nextjs", port: 3000, runCommand: "pnpm start --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000", }); // Read public_url from the response. Do not construct a production hostname. console.log(result); ``` **Python** ```python result = sandbox.deploy( name="hello-nextjs", path="/workspace/hello-nextjs", port=3000, run_command="pnpm start --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000", ) # Read public_url from the response. Do not construct a production hostname. print(result) ``` Always use the returned `public_url`. Do not construct a production hostname from the slug, Organization name, or Workspace name. **Expected result:** the response identifies the Deployment, candidate Release, promoted Version, and `public_url`. ## Step 5: Prove production A successful build is not enough. Confirm the Deployment resolved to a live Version and that the public URL answers. ```bash miosa deploy get hello-nextjs --json curl --fail --silent --show-error "$PUBLIC_URL" | grep "Hello from MIOSA" miosa deploy observe hello-nextjs ``` **Expected result:** the Deployment reports a running state with a `public_url`, the public response contains "Hello from MIOSA", and `observe` shows the request. ## Step 6: Connect a custom domain This step is optional. The platform URL remains valid while DNS is being configured. ```bash miosa deploy domain-add hello-nextjs app.example.com ``` MIOSA displays the required DNS record and verification target. Copy those values exactly into the DNS provider. For a normal subdomain, the record generally has this shape: | Type | Host | Value | Proxying | |---|---|---|---| | `CNAME` | `app` | The target shown by MIOSA | Disabled until verification completes | Do not copy `example.com` literally. Use a hostname controlled by the customer and the target displayed in the live MIOSA domain flow. Check public DNS, then verify: ```bash dig app.example.com CNAME +short miosa deploy domain-verify hello-nextjs ``` **Expected result:** the domain moves through DNS verification, certificate issuance, and routing until HTTPS is active. > **Caution: Wildcard and exact domains are different** > > An Organization-level deployment domain can generate many application hostnames beneath one parent domain. > An exact custom domain attaches one chosen hostname directly to one Deployment. > Follow the record shown for the domain type you selected. > See [Domains](/docs/docker-host/domains). ## Step 7: Publish an update safely Change the heading in `app/page.tsx`, rebuild in the Sandbox, and publish again. ```bash miosa exec hello-nextjs --cwd /workspace/hello-nextjs --timeout 300 -- pnpm build miosa deploy create \ --from-sandbox hello-nextjs \ --name hello-nextjs \ --dir /workspace/hello-nextjs \ --port 3000 \ --run-command "pnpm start --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000" \ --wait \ --json ``` Reusing `--name` targets the existing Deployment, so its identity, stable URL, domains, bindings, and release history are preserved while a new Version is promoted. Run the proof steps again after the new Version is promoted. ## Step 8: Understand rollback before you need it List the Deployment versions: ```bash miosa deploy versions hello-nextjs --json ``` If the new Version is unhealthy, return to the earlier ready one: ```bash miosa deploy rollback hello-nextjs --to ``` Rollback repoints the active Version in seconds without a rebuild. It does not change the Deployment identity or require a new domain. See [Rollback](/docs/docker-host/rollback). ## Common failures and recovery | Symptom | Likely cause | Safe action | Proof after repair | |---|---|---|---| | Sandbox creation remains pending | Requested capacity is not ready or the request is still progressing. | Inspect the readiness reason and wait or select compatible capacity. | The original Sandbox reaches a usable state. | | Preview returns an error | The Next.js process is stopped, bound to the wrong interface, or using another port. | Start it on `0.0.0.0:3000` with `miosa process start` and recreate the Preview. | The Preview returns "Hello from MIOSA." | | Publish reports Docker Host is unavailable | The Workspace Docker Host Host is not active. | Confirm the Workspace has an active Docker Host Host, then retry the same `miosa deploy create ... --type docker_deploy`. | Publish returns a Deployment and `public_url`. | | Build succeeds but the application is not live | Promotion, container health, or routing proof has not completed. | Inspect the publish result and run `miosa deploy get` and `miosa deploy observe`. | The public URL responds with the expected content. | | DNS remains pending | The record has not propagated, uses the wrong host, or points to the wrong target. | Compare public DNS with the exact record shown by MIOSA and keep proxying disabled during verification. | `miosa deploy domain-verify` reports DNS verified and TLS active. | | The custom hostname opens another application | The hostname was attached in the wrong Organization or to the wrong Deployment. | Stop and inspect ownership and route bindings before changing DNS again. | The domain resolves to the intended Deployment id and active Version. | | A new publish causes a regression | The candidate passed build but application behavior is incorrect. | Roll back to the earlier ready Version. | The stable URL serves the previous known-good content. | ## Completion checklist - [ ] The Sandbox exists in the intended Organization and Workspace. - [ ] The Next.js production build exits successfully. - [ ] The Preview displays "Hello from MIOSA." - [ ] Publishing returns a Deployment id and API-selected `public_url`. - [ ] The public URL returns the expected content. - [ ] The custom domain is verified and TLS-active, if configured. - [ ] An earlier ready Version is identifiable for rollback. - [ ] The Sandbox can be removed without deleting the Deployment. ## Continue from here - [Add Postgres](/docs/data/postgres): Bind durable application data without putting a database inside the application container. - [Add secrets](/docs/security/secrets): Provide sensitive runtime configuration without committing it to source. - [Understand publishing](/docs/docker-host/publishing): Learn the full Release, Version, promotion, proof, and retry contract. - [Operate domains](/docs/docker-host/domains): Configure deployment domains, exact custom domains, verification, TLS, and recovery. ## Next steps - [Publish from a sandbox](/docs/docker-host/publishing): Static, dynamic, and App Engine publishes with proof. - [Attach a custom domain](/docs/docker-host/domains): DNS verification, TLS, and route caching. - [Roll back in seconds](/docs/docker-host/rollback): Re-point a deployment at an older version with no rebuild. - [Return to Learning Paths](/docs/learn): Choose the agent, desktop, or white-label journey next.
